items.answer: q⁴ is the probability that the first 4 attempts are all failures, i.e. P(X > 4); P(X ≤ 4) = 1 − q⁴ = 0.821.

items.stem: A garden designer in Mumbai draws a flower bed in the shape of a sector OAB of a circle with centre O, radius 10 m and angle AOB = 2π/5 radians. (a) Find the exact area of the flower bed. (b) Yusuf enlarges the bed by increasing the radius to 12 m, keeping the same angle. Find the exact increase in area. (c) Find, in radians to 3 significant figures, the angle a sector of the same radius would need for an area of 20 m².
The function f is defined by f(x) = x² + 10x + 30 for x ≤ c. Find the greatest value of the constant c for which f is one-one, and state the range of f for this value of c.
items.markingKey: M1 completes the square or finds vertex x = −5; A1 c = −5; B1 range f(x) ≥ 5

items.stem: The curve C has equation y = x² − 1 and the line L has equation y = −5x + 5. (a) Find the x-coordinates of the points where L meets C. (b) Find the set of values of x for which y = x² − 1 is negative. (c) By completing the square, find the least value of y on C. (d) Find the set of values of x for which x² − 1 ≥ 8.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 equates and rearranges to x² + 5x − 6 = 0; A1 x = −6, 1 [2] (b) M1 roots −1, 1; A1 −1 < x < 1 [2] (c) M1 x² − 1; A1 least value −1 [2] (d) M1 x² ≥ 9; A1 x ≤ −3 or x ≥ 3 [2]

items.stem: The annual salaries, in thousands of dollars, of the 9 employees of a small company in Nairobi are: 22, 27, 31, 33, 36, 36, 36, 36, 110. (a) Calculate the mean salary. (b) State which average best represents the salary of a typical employee, giving a reason. (c) Find the mean salary of the other employees if the salary of 110 is excluded.
items.answer: (a) 40.8 (b) the median (36), as it is not affected by the outlier 110 (c) 32.1
items.markingKey: (a) M1 Σx = 367; A1 40.8 [2] (b) B1 median; B1 not affected by the extreme value [2] (c) M1 (367 − 110) ÷ 8; A1 32.1 [2]

items.stem: The function f is defined by f(x) = 5 − 4 cos x for 0 ≤ x ≤ π. (a) State the range of f. (b) Explain why f has an inverse. (c) Find an expression for f⁻¹(x). (d) State the domain of f⁻¹. (e) Solve the equation f(x) = 5.
items.answer: (a) 1 ≤ f(x) ≤ 9 (b) cos x is decreasing on 0 ≤ x ≤ π, so −cos x is increasing and f is one-one. (c) f⁻¹(x) = cos⁻¹((5 − x)/4) (d) 1 ≤ x ≤ 9 (e) x = π/2
items.markingKey: (a) B1 1 ≤ f(x) ≤ 9 [1] (b) B1 f is one-one (increasing) on the domain [1] (c) M1 cos x = (5 − y)/4; A1 f⁻¹(x) = cos⁻¹((5 − x)/4) [2] (d) B1 1 ≤ x ≤ 9 [1] (e) B1 cos x = 0 ⇒ x = π/2 [1]

items.stem: Water is poured into a conical container at 10 cm³ s⁻¹. When the depth is h cm, the volume is V = (2/3)πh³ cm³. Find the rate at which the depth is increasing when h = 6.

The points A(2, −2), B(1, −4) and C(−3, −2) are the vertices of a triangle. (a) Find the exact length of AC. (b) Find the equation of the line AC in the form ax + by + c = 0. (c) Find the area of triangle ABC.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 distance formula; A1 5 [2] (b) M1 gradient 0; A1 y + 2 = 0 [2] (c) M1 ½ × AB × BC; A1 5 [2]

items.stem: An arithmetic progression has first term 2 and common difference 3. The sum of the first n terms is 260. Find the value of n.
items.markingKey: M1 ½n(2 × 2 + (n − 1) × 3) = 260; M1 3n² + n − 520 = 0; A1 n = 13 (negative root rejected)

items.stem: The table summarises the distances, d km, travelled to work by 452 employees in Kathmandu: 0 ≤ d < 4: 6; 4 ≤ d < 10: 8; 10 ≤ d < 20: 120; 20 ≤ d < 40: 300; 40 ≤ d < 60: 18. (a) Calculate an estimate of the mean. (b) Calculate an estimate of the standard deviation. (c) A second sample of the same size from another city has mean 21.0 and standard deviation 7.1. Compare the two samples. (d) Explain why your answer for the standard deviation is an estimate.
items.answer: (a) 26.0 (b) 8.93 (c) the second sample has a lower mean and is less spread out (mean 26.0, sd 8.93 for the first sample) (d) The raw data are not known; midpoints are used for each class.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 midpoints; A1 26.0 [2] (b) M1 Σfx² = 342416; M1 Σfx²/452 − x̄²; A1 8.93 [3] (c) B1 compares means; B1 compares standard deviations [2] (d) B1 midpoints used [1]

items.stem: Mateo throws a biased coin 80 times. The probability of a head on each throw is 0.55. X is the number of heads. (a) Use the approximation to find P(X ≥ 46). (b) Use the approximation to find P(X < 43).
items.markingKey: (a) M1 continuity correction 45.5; M1 standardises; A1 0.368 [3] (b) M1 continuity correction 42.5; M1 standardises; A1 0.368 [3]

items.stem: Events A and B are independent. P(A) = 0.5 and P(A ∪ B) = 0.65. Find P(B).
items.markingKey: M1 0.5 + p − 0.5p = 0.65; M1 solves for p; A1 P(B) = 0.3

items.stem: A bag contains 5 red and 3 blue counters. 2 counters are taken at random without replacement. The random variable X is the number of red counters taken. (a) Draw up the probability distribution table for X. (b) Find Var(X).
items.markingKey: (a) B1 values; M1 probabilities; A1 all correct [3] (b) M1 E(X²) − [E(X)]²; A1 45/112 (≈ 0.402) [2]

items.stem: For the curve y = x² + 3x, calculate the gradients of the chords from the point where x = 3 to the points where x = 3.1, 3.01, 3.001. Hence suggest the gradient of the curve at x = 3.
items.markingKey: M1 uses (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁); A1 9.1; A1 9.01; A1 9.001; B1 suggests 9

items.stem: X ~ B(5, 0.2). Find P(X = 2), correct to 3 significant figures.
When constructing a probability distribution, a useful check is that
items.markingKey: All possible values must be covered.

items.stem: 4 people are chosen at random from 4 men and 8 women. Mateo calculates the probability of exactly 3 women as (8/12)³ × (4/12). Give two reasons why this is wrong, and find the correct probability.
items.answer: The people are chosen without replacement, so the probabilities change; also the different orders of choosing are not counted. Correct: 8C3 × 4C1/12C4 = 224/495 (≈ 0.453).
items.markingKey: B1 without replacement / not independent; B1 orders not counted; B1 224/495 (≈ 0.453)

items.stem: For 58 values of x, Σx = 2042 and Σx² = 84852. Find the mean and the standard deviation of x.
Freya says a line perpendicular to a line of gradient −1/3 has gradient 1/3. Explain the error and give the correct gradient.
items.answer: Perpendicular gradients satisfy m₁m₂ = −1; −1/3 × 1/3 = −1/9 ≠ −1. Correct gradient 3.
items.markingKey: B1 m₁m₂ = −1 (check fails); B1 3

items.stem: Consider the expansion of (2 + 3x)⁷. (a) Find the first three terms in ascending powers of x. (b) Find the coefficient of x² in the expansion of (1 + x)(2 + 3x)⁷. (c) State the number of terms in the full expansion.

A closed cylindrical can has volume 500 cm³ and radius r cm, so that its surface area is A = 2πr² + 1000/r. Find the value of r that minimises A, and the minimum surface area, giving answers to 3 significant figures.
items.markingKey: M1 dA/dr = 4πr − 1000/r²; M1 = 0 ⇒ r³ = 250/π; A1 r = 4.30; M1 d²A/dr² > 0 (minimum); A1 A = 349

items.stem: Two fair eight-sided dice, numbered 1 to 8, are thrown. Event A is "the sum of the scores is a prime number" and event B is "the sum of the scores is greater than 13". (a) Find P(A) and P(B). (b) Determine whether A and B are independent. (c) Find P(A ∪ B). (d) Find P(A′ ∩ B′).
items.markingKey: (a) B1 P(A) = 23/64; B1 P(B) = 3/32 [2] (b) M1 compares P(A ∩ B) with P(A)P(B); A1 conclusion [2] (c) M1 addition law; A1 29/64 [2] (d) M1 1 − P(A ∪ B); A1 35/64 [2]

items.stem: The curve C has equation y = x − 5√x + 4, for x ≥ 0. (a) Find the x-coordinates of the points where C meets the line y = 0. (b) By writing y in the form (√x − p)² + q, find the least value of y and the value of x at which it occurs.
items.answer: (a) x = 1 or x = 16 (b) least value −9/4 when x = 25/4

items.stem: The masses, x grams, of 48 bags of flour are coded using y = (x − 500)/10. Given that Σy = −72, find the mean mass of the bags.
The function f is defined by f(x) = x² − 6x for x ≥ 3. (a) Express f(x) in the form (x − a)² + b. (b) State the range of f. (c) Solve the equation f(x) = f⁻¹(x).
items.markingKey: (a) B1 a = 3; B1 b = −9 [2] (b) B1 f(x) ≥ −9 [1] (c) M1 sets f(x) = x; A1 x² − 7x = 0; A1 x = 7 (x = 0 rejected, not in domain) [3]

items.stem: For the curve y = x² + 6x, calculate the gradients of the chords from the point where x = 0 to the points where x = 0.1, 0.01, 0.001. Hence suggest the gradient of the curve at x = 0.
items.markingKey: M1 uses (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁); A1 6.1; A1 6.01; A1 6.001; B1 suggests 6

items.stem: Two groups of 15 students sat the same test. Group X scores: 30, 30, 33, 50, 52, 54, 54, 59, 62, 64, 65, 65, 76, 77, 78. Group Y scores: 20, 29, 34, 48, 48, 50, 55, 56, 56, 59, 59, 67, 68, 76, 79. (a) Suggest a suitable diagram to compare the two groups, with a reason. (b) Find the median and IQR of each group. (c) Compare the performance of the two groups.
items.answer: (a) back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram (small data sets, keeps values, direct comparison) or two box plots (b) X: median 59, IQR 15; Y: median 56, IQR 19 (c) X has the higher median, so performed better on average; Y is more spread out.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 suitable diagram; B1 reason [2] (b) B1 medians; B1 quartiles; B1 IQRs [3] (c) B1 average comparison; B1 spread comparison [2]

items.stem: A curve has gradient function dy/dx = 4/√(3x + 10) and passes through P(2, 8). (a) Find the equation of the curve. (b) Find the equation of the normal to the curve at P, in the form ax + by + c = 0.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 integrates; A1 8/3√(3x + 10); M1 uses P; A1 c = −8/3 [4] (b) M1 gradient −1; A1 x + y − 10 = 0 [2]

items.stem: The equation 3 sin²x = −7 cos x + 5 is to be solved for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°. (a) Solve the equation for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°. (b) Prove the identity (1 − cos x)(1 + cos x) ≡ sin²x. (c) Explain why, in this equation, any value of cos x outside −1 ≤ cos x ≤ 1 is rejected.
items.answer: (a) 70.5°, 289.5° (b) Expand: 1 − cos²x = sin²x. (c) The range of cos x is −1 to 1, so such values give no angles.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 factorises/solves the quadratic: cos x = 1/3 (cos x = 2 rejected); A1 one angle; A1 all angles 70.5°, 289.5° [3] (b) B1 expands and uses the identity [1] (c) B1 range of cosine [1]
